11.title: Physical World & Units and Measurement
11.summary: Focus heavily on dimensional formulas of constants (G, h, η, permeability), checking the consistency of physical equations, and propagation of percentage errors (ΔZ/Z = a·ΔA/A + b·ΔB/B).

questions.question: What is the dimensional formula for the Universal Gravitational Constant (G)?
questions.explanation: From F = G(m₁m₂)/r², G = F·r²/(m₁m₂). Substituting dimensions: [M L T⁻²][L²] / [M²] = [M⁻¹ L³ T⁻²].

11.title: Laws of Motion
11.summary: Revise Free Body Diagrams (FBD), impulse theorem (J = Δp = F·Δt), apparent weight in an elevator, and maximum friction force f_max = μ_s · N.

questions.question: A 2kg block rests on a rough horizontal floor (μs = 0.4). If a 5N force is applied horizontally, the static friction force is:
questions.explanation: Limiting friction f_max = μs·m·g = 0.4 × 2 × 9.8 = 7.84 N. Because applied force (5N) is less than limiting friction, static friction self-adjusts to equal 5 N.

12.title: Electric Charges and Fields
12.summary: Crucial topics: Coulomb's Law in vector form, torque on a dipole (τ = p × E), potential energy (U = -p · E), and Gauss's Law applications for thin wire, infinite plane sheet, and spherical shell.

questions.question: An electric dipole of moment p is placed in a uniform electric field E. The torque experienced by it is maximum when the angle between p and E is:
questions.explanation: Torque is given by τ = pE sin(θ). The sine function attains its maximum value of 1 when θ = 90°.

questions.question: If the radius of a Gaussian sphere enclosing a point charge is doubled, the electric flux passing through the sphere:
questions.explanation: By Gauss's Law, Φ = Q_enclosed / ε₀. Flux depends strictly on the net enclosed charge, not on the dimensions of the Gaussian surface.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of electric flux?
questions.explanation: Flux Φ = E · A = (Force / Charge) × Area = (N/C) × m² = N m² / C (also equivalent to Volt·meter).

12.title: Current Electricity
12.summary: High probability: Drift velocity relation (I = n·e·A·v_d), temperature coefficient of resistance, Kirchhoff's Junction & Loop rules, and Wheatstone bridge balance condition.

questions.question: Two resistors of 3 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in parallel across an ideal 6V battery. The total current drawn from the battery is:
questions.explanation: Parallel resistance: R_eq = (3 × 6) / (3 + 6) = 18 / 9 = 2 Ω. Current I = V / R_eq = 6V / 2Ω = 3 A.
